append.text: **Ps 11:7, the first *elóquium* outside Ps 118 (D26 asked for a local decision): *Elóquia Dómini, elóquia casta* → *As palavras do Senhor são palavras puras*.** Why *palavra* here: the clause cannot repeat as a predicate (the Latin's figure is the noun said twice), so it would drop a repetition (rule 2); draft 1's *Os ditos do Senhor são ditos castos* was refused by the stylist ("máximas moralmente recatadas") — the ninth refusal of plural *ditos*, now with a genitive and an adjective — and the blind reader paraphrased it *palavras puras*; the psalm has no *verbum* or *sermo*, so nothing collides; DRB and MS1932 have *words*. The Latinist passed both drafts. **17:31 *elóquia Dómini igne examináta* should follow (*as palavras do Senhor examinadas no fogo*); 147:4 (*elóquium* + *sermo* in one verse) and 106:11 must still decide locally.** Options kept in Ps 11: *ditos castos / puros*, the clause *O que o Senhor disse é puro*.

**Ps 11:3–4 *lábia dolósa* twice → *lábios enganadores* both times** (one decision, two slots); in 11:3 *com* is supplied (*com lábios enganadores*) so that the lips are not heard as the subject of *falaram*. No reader remarked on the adjective.
Ps 11:4 *Extermine o Senhor todos os lábios enganadores* — the jussive with the subject after it; the blind reader heard "destroy the people who deceive".
Ps 11:2 *Salvai-me, Senhor* — the formula *Salvum me fac, Dómine* (also 117:25 *O Dómine, salvum me fac*).
Ps 11:5 *Engrandeceremos a nossa língua* (the boast in the Latin's image; MS1932 explains it) — echoed by 11:4 *magníloquam* → *que fala grandezas*.

**Ps 11:2 *quóniam defécit sanctus*: *desfalecer* fails with a person as subject meaning "is gone"** ("the holy man fainted"). *desapareceu o santo* (draft 1) was heard as one particular person's death → ***porque já não há santo*** (DRB "there is now no saint"), heard generically. **Stands against the Latinist (major, draft 2), who wants the perfect back** — held: resultative perfect, both Vulgate-family versions have the present state. The other *defécit* (30:11, 54:12, 72:26, 76:4, 106:5, 142:7a *defécit spíritus meus*) have things as subject and may keep *desfalecer*.
Ps 11:6b *Ponam in salutári* → *Porei na salvação* (no object, as the Latin; the blind reader supplied "the poor" without stumbling, twice).

**Ps 11:8, the place this row named: *servábis nos: et custódies nos* → *nos conservareis: e nos guardareis*** — with a person as object *serváre* is *conservar* (the verb of the blessing *Deus vos conserve*); *custodíre* keeps *guardar*; no reader remarked. Options *preservareis*, MS1932's order (*guardareis … preservareis*).
Ps 11:8 *desta geração para sempre* — D23 applied.
Ps 11:6a *agora me levantarei, diz o Senhor* (God speaking of himself); heard as "now I will act for the poor".
Ps 11:3 *vana* (neuter plural) → *coisas vãs* too; the blind reader listed *vãs* as unknown twice.

terms: | inops / pauper / egénus | indigente / pobre / (necessitado) | open | Ps 11:6a *Por causa da miséria dos indigentes, e do gemido dos pobres*. The Latin keeps three words (and *mendícus*, 39:18, 108:17) and pairs them constantly: *inops* 14 lines (13:6, 34:10, 36:14, 71:13, 73:21 *pauper et inops*, 85:1 *inops, et pauper sum ego*, 108:17, 112:7, 139:13 …), *egénus* 6 (34:10, 40:2, 69:6, 81:3–4, 108:22 — grep). Proposed: *pauper → pobre*; *inops* ("without means") → *indigente*, whose noun *indigência* serves *inópia* (33:10, 43:24, 87:9, 106:41); *egénus → necessitado*, reserved. **The blind reader listed *indigentes* as unknown twice**; options *desvalidos* (MS1932), *necessitados*. The stylist named 11:6a the psalm's best line |

| magníloquus | que fala grandezas (*e a língua que fala grandezas*) | open | Ps 11:4 only (grep); L&S "vaunting, boastful" (citing this verse), μεγαλορήμων. Keeps *magni-* and *-loquus*, and echoes 11:5 *magnificábimus* → *Engrandeceremos*. **The Latinist asked twice (minor) for the boasting to be explicit** — *com arrogância* (MS1932), then *com altivez*; refused: both blind readings heard boasting first |

| castus | puro (*palavras puras*) | open | Ps 11:7 only (grep); ἁγνός. *castas* was heard by the blind reader as sexual chastity and listed as unknown; *puro* meets *mundus* (50:12 *cor mundum*) in no verse. MS1932 *sinceras* is *sincérus*'s |

| examináre / probáre | examinar / provar (*prata examinada no fogo, provada, purificada da terra sete vezes*) | open | Ps 11:7; **65:10 sets them side by side** (*probásti nos, Deus: igne nos examinásti, sicut examinátur argéntum*), so two verbs; *provar* also 16:3, 25:2, 138:23 *Proba me*. L&S *examino* "to weigh, test". *provada no fogo* is the idiom but would give *provar* to *examináre*. 17:31 *igne examináta* follows. *terræ* left where it can hang on either participle (DRB *purged from the earth*; MS1932's *no crisol* interprets) |

| fiduciáliter (ágere) | com confiança (*nele agirei com confiança*) | open | Ps 11:6b only (L&S cite it); παρρησιάσομαι. *nele* as open as *in eo*. The blind reader heard the colon as the psalmist's, twice — the Latin marks the Lord's words off no better. MS1932 *confiadamente* |

| diminúere, *diminútæ sunt* | diminuir, intransitive (*diminuíram as verdades*) | open | Ps 11:2 only; ὠλιγώθησαν "became few"; the intransitive for a medio-passive, as *se elevou* (8:2b). The Latinist passed it on draft 1 and marked the voice on draft 2, words unchanged; *foram diminuídas* and *minguaram* are options |

| altitúdo | altura (*segundo a vossa altura*) | open | Ps 11:9 (of God); 55:4, 68:3 *altitúdinem maris*, 94:4 *altitúdines móntium*, 102:11 *secúndum altitúdinem cæli* (grep) — the concrete word everywhere; *alteza* is a royal title; the blind reader heard "greatness" first |

| in circúitu | ao redor (de) | working | Ps 11:9 *Os ímpios andam ao redor* (no *de nós*, which MS1932 adds); 15 lines (grep), most with a genitive: 33:8, 49:3, 88:9 *véritas tua in circúitu tuo*, 124:2b, 127:3b *in circúitu mensæ tuæ* |

| próximus | próximo | working | Ps 11:3; a proparoxytone: at a cadence it needs a word after it (11:3 was recast so that the mediant falls on *coisas vãs*); 14:3b, 14:4b, 23:4, 27:3, 34:14, 37:12 (grep) |
| lábia … a nobis sunt | os nossos lábios são nossos | open | Ps 11:5; possession (DRB *our own*, MS1932 *somos donos*); the Latinist (draft 2, minor) prefers origin, *vêm de nós* — option |

| in corde et corde | com um coração e outro coração | open | Ps 11:3 only; the Hebrew idiom carried word for word by the Greek and the Latin. Draft 1 *com coração e coração* was heard by the blind reader as possibly *de coração para coração* (sincerity — the opposite); *um … outro* keeps both nouns and was heard as duplicity. DRB, DM1962 *duplo coração* and MS1932 *coração dúplice* explain |
| séptuplum | sete vezes | working | Ps 11:7 (DRB, MS1932); 78:12 *redde … séptuplum* is a noun (*sete vezes mais*) and decides there |
formulas: | *Elóquia Dómini … igne examináta* (11:7 *Elóquia Dómini, elóquia casta: argéntum igne examinátum*; 17:31 *elóquia Dómini igne examináta*) | *As palavras do Senhor … examinada(s) no fogo* | open — Ps 11 (D26 decided locally for *palavra*, reasons in the *verbum / sermo / elóquium* row); **Ps 17:31 should copy it** |
